standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with the resolution property has affine diagonal
On a scheme with affine diagonal a morphism of perfect objects is represented by a roof with quasi-coherent middle term
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the roof E <- H -> F with H quasi-coherent and H -> E a quasi-isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Because E and F are bounded, the roof maps factor through a truncation of H, allowing H to be replaced by a bounded below complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Prepares the input for the strictly perfect construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: The strictly perfect construction lemma replaces a bounded below quasi-coherent middle term by a bounded complex of finite locally free modules

core_obligations: Deduce affine diagonal and represent alpha by a roof E <- H -> F where H is a complex of quasi-coherent modules and H -> E is a quasi-isomorphism, via the resolution-property affine-diagonal lemma and the quasi-compact affine-diagonal proposition (proof lines 9928-9938).
For n << 0 the maps H -> E and H -> F factor through the quasi-isomorphism H -> tau_{>= n} H because E and F are bounded; replace H by tau_{>= n} H, making it bounded below (proof lines 9938-9946).
Apply the strictly perfect construction lemma to conclude that G = tau_{>= n} H can be taken to be a bounded complex of finite locally free modules (proof lines 9947-9948).
proof_roadmap: Represent alpha by a quasi-coherent roof using the affine diagonal (proof lines 9928-9938).
Truncate the middle term to a bounded below complex (proof lines 9938-9946).
Replace it by a bounded finite locally free complex (proof lines 9947-9948).
